deities: Bhagavan Manguesh (Shiva, worshipped as a Shiva lingam)

history.dynasty: Maratha-era rebuild; original temple predates Portuguese conquest of Salcette
history.period: Origins ancient; present structure built from mid-18th century onward
history.summary: The original temple stood at Kushasthali (later Cortalim), on the south bank of the Zuari river in Salcette. After the Portuguese conquest of Salcette in 1543 and the start of conversions around 1560, the Saraswats of Vatsa gotra shifted the Mangesh lingam to Mangeshi in Priol, Ponda, then outside Portuguese control. The Peshwa Sardar Ramchandra Malhar Sukhtankar, a devotee of Mangesh, donated the village of Mangeshi to the temple in 1739; the current edifice was built under Maratha rule (c. 1744 per some sources) and renovated again in 1890 and 1973, when a golden kalash was installed atop the dome. Mythology holds that Shiva became 'Manguesh' (Mam Girisha) after Parvati cried 'Trahi Mam Girisha' (O Lord of the Mountains, save me) when he frightened her in tiger form. Lata Mangeshkar's family is associated with the village. DUPLICATE ROW: this is the same temple as CSV seq 221 ('Shree Mangeshi', handled by another worker) — keep-or-drop decision needed. CSV town corrected from 'Ponda' to 'Mangeshi' (Mangeshi is a village within Priol, Ponda taluka, ~21 km from Panaji).

name: Shri Mangueshi Temple
town_description: Mangeshi is a village within Priol in Ponda taluka, North Goa, 21–22 km from Panaji. It is one of Goa's most visited temple towns, home to the wealthy and popular Mangueshi Shiva temple.
tradition: Hindu (Shaiva; Manguesh is a form of Shiva recognized only in Goa)

travel.railway: Karmali (nearest); Vasco da Gama ~37 km; Margao ~26 km
travel.road: On Dinanath Mangeshkar Road at Mangeshi, Priol; ~21 km from Panaji Kadamba Bus Stand

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Mahashivratri and the annual Jatra draw the largest crowds
